newsitem.title: USA: Vita Food sees higher Q4 pretax income.
newsitem.headline: Vita Food sees higher Q4 pretax income.

text.p: Vita Food Products Inc said Tuesday it expects to report fourth quarter income that will be "very modestly" lower compared to the $886,000 or $0.30 a share it earned in the 1995 quarter.
The 1996 quarter, however, included the payment of income taxes compared with no taxes paid laxt year.
On a pretax basis, fourth quarter 1996 earnings will be up about 20 percent from the 1995 period, Vita Food said.
"On a pretax basis, the comparisons are much better," Jay Dembsky, chief financial officer, said in an interview. "We're expecting pretax income (will be) up about 20 percent."
Revenues for the fourth quarter are expected to be up about two to five percent from year-ago revenues of $8.4 million, Dembsky said.
For the year, which ended December 31, 1996, Vita Food said it expects to report revenues of between $22.0 and $23.0 million, compared with 1995 revenues of $21.4 million.
Net income for the year, Dembsky said, is expected to be between $700,000 and $850,000, or roughly $0.24 to $0.29 a share. A year ago, it earned $131,000 or $0.04 a share.
The 1995 results, however, included a $356,000 litigation settlement charge, which reduced net income by about $0.12 a share.
Adding that charge to 1995 earnings, Dembsky said, "it's still a strong" comparison for 1996.
For the first nine months of 1996, Vita Food reported a net loss of $27,997 or $0.01 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $754,645 or $0.26 a share.
